title: Liposomal Encapsulation of Camcholate, a Marine Catecholate Siderophore, for Fluorescence-Based Bioimaging in Artemia nauplii
authors: V Archana; VP Limna Mol; TC Sreelatha; K b . Revathi; G Dharani
abstract: Abstract We report the chemical synthesis of Camcholate, a catecholate siderophore, its loading into liposomes, and a test of its use as a fluorescent bioimaging agent in the brine shrimp Artemia salina. Camcholate was made by peptide coupling of 2,3-dihydroxybenzoic acid to an amino acid frame, giving a catecholate–amide structure similar to enterobactin [1]. The purified product was characterised by FTIR (broad O–H/N–H stretch and strong amide C = O bands at 1678 and 1657 cm⁻¹), ¹H and ¹³C NMR (aromatic signals at δ 6.9–7.5, amide NH at δ 7.8–8.5, aliphatic CH at δ 4.7 and CH₃ at δ 1.48), and high-resolution ESI-MS, which gave [M + H]⁺ at m/z 387.1531, consistent with C₂₀H₂₃N₂O₆. Camcholate was encapsulated in phosphatidylcholine–cholesterol liposomes by thin-film hydration. Dynamic light scattering gave a mean diameter of about 125 nm, and SEM showed spherical vesicles of 100–150 nm. No mortality was seen in a brine shrimp lethality assay at 1–100 µg/mL. Under UV excitation, liposomal Camcholate gave bright fluorescence in the gut of Artemia nauplii (Fig. 8), where it remained visible for up to 120 min. These results show that synthetic Camcholate can be formulated into stable, biocompatible liposomes and used to follow ingested particles in a small aquatic model, which makes it a candidate imaging agent for nanomedicine.

title: Monolithic tiered microlithography for stretchable multilayer electronics with high-density, soft, and ultrathin VIAs
authors: Xinjian Xie; Guangrui Ju; Xiongwei Luo; Shengwei Feng; Hongjiao Li; Yijun Zhang; Wenqian Feng
abstract: Stretchable multilayer electronics that sustain reliable electrical performance under mechanical deformation are critical for advanced skin-like devices. A remaining challenge is the development of high-density, soft, and ultrathin vertical interconnect accesses (VIAs) that enable reliable electrical interconnection in flexible and stretchable circuits, particularly at small feature sizes. Here, we present a three-dimensional (3D), tier-by-tier photolithography strategy using PEDOT-based conductors and polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS)–based insulators, each photocurable within 10 seconds, to directly pattern soft VIAs and planar interconnects across lithographically defined PDMS openings. Maskless, full-field exposure enables thousands of in-plane and through-plane electrical connections in a single step, bypassing conventional hole-by-hole fabrication and manual VIA-to-pad alignment. The multilayer stack ensures minimal thickness, matched mechanical compliance, and robust conduction and insulation, enabling soft VIAs to preserve cross-layer electrical performance. Integration of lithographically defined cutouts and perforations yields breathable, conformal bioelectronics with skin-friendliness and stable signal acquisition in wearable wireless ECG monitoring. This multilayer 3D electronics platform can be extended to biomolecular sensing in soft organs, where thin, integrated, and stretchable designs are essential.

title: Integrating data management and analysis in bioimaging: A core facility perspective
authors: Lu Cao; Maarten W. Paul; Joost Willemse; Lenard M. Voortman; Tooba Abbassi‐Daloii; Katherine Wolstencroft; Sylvia Le Dévédec
abstract: Abstract Bioimaging core facilities increasingly operate at the centre of data‐intensive biological research. Advances in microscopy instrumentation, automation, image analysis, and multimodal workflows have increased the scale, complexity, and institutional importance of imaging data. At the same time, the scientific community embraces the FAIR principles, which require data to be Findable, Accessible, Interoperable, and Reusable. Existing literature provides foundational guidance in discrete domains such as data stewardship, metadata standards, data storage and visualisation, workflow integration, and community file formats. However, a comprehensive view that unifies these domains from the perspective of an imaging core facility is missing. This review fills that gap by proposing an integrated model for modern imaging data ecosystems. We connect/integrate developments in metadata standards, cloud‐native file formats, workflow orchestration frameworks, AI reproducibility, and multimodal data integration. We explore the organisational and governance challenges that shape institutional adoption and sustainability, and present facility‐level strategies for transforming imaging data management and analysis into a coherent, future‐proof ecosystem.

title: Iontronic triboelectric tele-perception enabled by ion-relaxation engineering and a lightweight 1D-CNN decoder
authors: Jiaxin Guo; Yan Du; Zhong Lin Wang; Di Wei
abstract: Abstract Robots must recognize what is approaching before they touch it. Triboelectric tele-perception meets this need, but its responses stay pinned to the material permittivity (dielectric constant) of the target: the voltage waveform collapses to a scaled copy of the electrostatic coupling, and material identity must then be recovered from a handful of amplitudes. We show that ionic relaxation in an iontronic dielectric breaks this constraint. Dispersing room temperature ionic liquid of BMIMTFSI (10 wt%) in thermoplastic polyurethane (TPU) gives an iontronic triboelectric sensor (ITS) whose mobile ions relax on the time scale of an approach event, so that ionic polarization and electrostatic induction act as two independent contributions to the same voltage transient. The resulting waveforms differ in shape, not merely in height: the iontronic film retains 91.57% of its initial output after 10⁵ cycles and resolves four target materials as distinct polarity-amplitude classes at 70 mm. Because the discriminating information lies in the waveform morphology, a generic one-dimensional convolutional neural network (1D-CNN) fed with raw voltage traces classifies the four materials at 90.5% mean accuracy without hand-crafted features. We use this output to drive material-specific robot motions and a polarity-gated three-level warning display. Ionic relaxation thus supplies a design degree of freedom that is orthogonal to permittivity, and it turns an electrostatic proximity signal into a material fingerprint that a small decoder can read.

title: Intraoperative Indocyanine Green Fluorescence Imaging in Pancreatic Head and Periampullary Surgery: A Scoping Review
authors: Loizos Hadjigeorgiou; Dimitra Sertidou; Spiros G. Delis; Vasileios Tatsis; Evangelos Lolis; Konstantinos Vlachos; Georgios K. Glantzounis
abstract: Background/Objectives: Indocyanine green (ICG) fluorescence imaging is inexpensive and increasingly used in pancreatic surgery, but its evidence base has been appraised only in fragments—one application at a time, or ICG pooled with investigational fluorophores—and never specifically for the pancreatic head and periampullary region. We mapped its intraoperative applications, techniques and reported outcomes. Methods: Following the PRISMA-ScR guidelines, we searched PubMed, Scopus, the Cochrane Library and the Directory of Open Access Journals on 29 July 2026 without date restriction. Two reviewers screened and charted independently, one row per article-by-application combination, and synthesised the findings narratively. Results: Forty-two studies (51 article-by-application combinations, 613 patients) covered six applications: stump perfusion, biliary identification and anastomotic testing, perfusion of reconstructed vessels and the duodenal arcade, tumour detection and margin assessment, lymphatic mapping, and staging laparoscopy. Eighteen were case or technique reports, no randomised trial was identified, and only three studies included a group operated without ICG. Remnant hypoperfusion predicted postoperative acute pancreatitis (80% versus 16%, p = 0.011) and clinically relevant fistula (odds ratio 10.0) in two small prospective cohorts, yet in the largest series (n = 100) a visual score of the pancreaticojejunostomy was reproducible (intraclass correlation coefficient 0.76) but discriminated poorly (area under the curve 0.64) and altered no operation. In a single retrospective comparison in duodenum-preserving resection, ICG guidance was associated with less intraoperative bile-duct injury (10% versus 60%, p = 0.009). Conventional doses did not distinguish pancreatic adenocarcinoma from normal parenchyma, whereas second-window imaging made 12 of 13 invasive specimens fluoresce. Dose varied by two orders of magnitude, and no adverse reaction was reported, although tolerability was formally assessed in only nine studies. Conclusions: Intraoperative ICG use in pancreatic head surgery appears safe and feasible. ICG shows key anatomical structures—above all the biliary tree—more reliably than white light alone. Its most promising benefits are the early recognition of an ischaemic pancreatic remnant, with the prospect of preventing postoperative fistula and pancreatitis, and the early identification and protection of the distal bile duct during duodenum-preserving pancreatic head resection.

title: Solubility-driven morphological decoupling enables elastic electron-deficient semiconducting polymers for fully stretchable electronics
authors: Hayeong Park; Qian Liu; Wenhao Li; Minji Chung; Gunmo Koo; Chien-Chung Shih; Christopher R. McNeill; Dongsheng Yan; Yang Wang; Shanshan Zhou; Mandar M. Shirolkar; Ruicheng Li; Aung Ko Ko Kyaw; Yunqi Liu; Prashant Sonar; Joon Hak Oh
abstract: The development of fully stretchable electronics is limited by the scarcity of electron-deficient polymers that combine high electron mobility with mechanical elasticity. Here, we report a solubility-driven morphological decoupling strategy that mitigates this trade-off by incorporating ∼10% planar, insoluble PyF units into a semicrystalline PySe backbone. This approach yields a hierarchical morphology characterized by suppressed long-range crystallinity alongside robust local aggregation. Driven by strong fluorine (F)-sulfur (S) interactions, highly ordered face-on domains function as robust physical anchors, providing the polymer network with exceptional elasticity to reversibly dissipate stress and preserve charge percolation pathways. Consequently, the resulting terpolymer largely relieves the long-standing trade-off between charge transport and mechanical stretchability, delivering a near-unity initial electron mobility (∼1.0 square centimeter per volt per second) and retaining 0.5 square centimeters per volt per second even under 100% applied strain, representing the highest performance reported to date. To demonstrate the practical utility of this system, we fabricated stretchable ambipolar inverters and phototransistors that maintain high performance under severe deformation. Notably, the phototransistors sustain an exceptional responsivity of 15.8 amperes per watt and an external quantum efficiency exceeding 2900% at 100% strain. These results establish a powerful blueprint for intrinsically elastic semiconductors, enabling the realization of high-performance, fully deformable optoelectronic systems.

title: Multifunctional, Tough, and Highly Stretchable Aramid Nanofiber Reinforced Conductive Hydrogel for Wearable Electronics
authors: Qifa Gou; Yadong Chen; Jipeng Wang; Chang Wu; Longbiao Yuan; Zihao Gao; Jianmin Guo; Xuelei Wang; Li Ke; Qiang Du; Tianxing Gong; Chongshu Wang; Shibo Wei
abstract: Abstract Flexible strain sensors require stable, sensitive, and repeatable signal acquisition during complex motions, and hydrogels have emerged as promising candidates for this purpose. In this study, a fiber-reinforced ionic conductive hydrogel was constructed by introducing an aramid nanofiber (ANF) reinforcing framework and a dynamic Zn2+ coordination network. ANF enhanced stress transfer and load-bearing capacity, while reversible Zn2+ coordination crosslinks provided energy dissipation and stable ionic conductive pathways. The resulting hydrogel exhibited a tensile strength of 2.22 MPa, fracture strain of 800%, toughness of 9.58 MJ m−3, and electrical conductivity of 0.66 S m−1. Moreover, it showed reliable resistance responses to tensile and compressive stimuli, with tensile and compressive gauge factors (GF) of 6.94 and 8.4, respectively. The synergistic design of ANF reinforcement and Zn2+ coordination effectively balances mechanical performance, conductivity, and sensing sensitivity, offering a feasible strategy for flexible electronics and wearable sensors.
